answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously, adding one per fatigue and one for Chairman. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. Move the member to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.

evidence.quote: Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire.

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner select one card each (take or discard), descending by actual total retirement spending. Ties: more total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Do not replace cards during selection; if display empties skip remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if none was taken. Return unused pensioners to supplies.

evidence.quote: Players who retired at least one pensioner must each take or discard one display card

answers.answer: Check the marker's location at phase start. Take a main action once, or twice if it already matched; then move marker to the chosen action. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action, never doubled and never moving the marker. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer's once-this-turn bonus adds one writer: doubled Writer action can place three total.

evidence.quote: Check where your opportunity marker was at phase start

answers.answer: After all family actions, while Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat. With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Applicants become shares only in Court. Seek Share paid the printed queue cost to the bank, never to Company treasuries.

evidence.quote: With no Debt, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on card backs. For own-family hiring, obtain verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool (Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt). On promotion transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card as vacant in ascending order. If candidate or hirer is unavailable, skip it; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

evidence.quote: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on their card backs.

answers.answer: Former Chairman announces the number needed for a pure majority (> half current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; first candidate backed by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody has the support, former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self, without Nepotism consent. Elected member's share moves to Chairman slot but still counts for dividends, majority and scoring; it cannot be traded or invested in firms.

evidence.quote: Former Chairman first announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority

answers.answer: Commit resources/cash first; Company-office check cash must come from the acting office treasury and is paid to bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, roll and use the lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure, retry if resources and office limits allow; 5–6 catastrophe, ending that office's actions, returning officeholder to supply, discarding fatigue and flipping card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm procedures modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success.

evidence.quote: Use lowest die: 1–2 success; 3–4 failure

answers.answer: Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 Balance. Each further advance needs consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); never pass Debt track end. Then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, lowering Balance by transfers. Borrowing and allocation may be interleaved subject to limits; cash already in offices remains there.

evidence.quote: May add up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance.

answers.answer: Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. Lease extra ship £2; fit a ship from a shipyard £3 without owner consent; buy a Company ship £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China if created. Extra ships return at Refresh.

evidence.quote: Must spend treasury until £2 or less remains.

answers.answer: Declare home plus regions reachable through open orders within available ship capacity; pay £1 from President treasury per die and subtract one die per declared nonhome region. Successful Trade fills at most one order per ship in that Presidency sea zone; first writer to home, every later fill extends this Trade's connected route. Other-Presidency writers cannot extend it. Writers do not cap capacity: use them then filled-order tokens for remaining ships. Cannot fill another President's home even if vacant. Company gets printed order value, or half rounded down if firm filled it this turn; President gets £1/order, writer owners £1/writer. At most one successful Trade per President/turn; failed retries stay in its uninterrupted opportunity.

evidence.quote: Successful Trade capacity is one order per ship in this Presidency’s sea zone.

answers.answer: Target own Presidency home, associated region, or region bordering an associated region; not another home or another Presidency's Company region. A Company target must have unrest or a closed order. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for printed dice, then subtract target plus all other regions in target's empire (target counted once; Company defense is zero). A noncatastrophic failure can retry with remaining resources. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted; each 6 removes that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll loss dice.

evidence.quote: After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in attempt

answers.answer: Loot from bank is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, minimum surviving participating officers +1 for Commander. Count only this attempt's survivors and used regiments/alliances. Repeated payout cycles: Commander family £1 for Commander plus each used surviving officer; other families clockwise £1/used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment/alliance piece, stopping each cycle when cash runs out. Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower/dome (and all matching flags if capital), open all orders/clear unrest; on new conquest orient token region-symbol up above associated President box, put Governor overlay in region and only Governor card in Vacant Offices. If outward-facing Elephant, move inside. Catastrophe: Commander returns half own family trophies rounded up and member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.

evidence.quote: £4 per target tower + faceup loot modifier

answers.answer: Use printed dice pool; each attempt rolls current pool without penalty and reduces it by one regardless. Success: take £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll failed, then choose exactly one: build ship one stage (place partial ship in region, or if already partial complete into associated President's sea zone), commission regiment into that President's Army, or add unsplit £2 to Balance or that President's treasury. Each Tax after first this turn adds regional unrest. Any unsuccessful roll adds unrest; catastrophe also removes officeholder. Repeat with shrinking pool until stop, no dice or catastrophe.

evidence.quote: Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one

answers.answer: Expenses are £1 per existing Debt, each Army officer/regiment, each ship in sea zones including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance is short, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt only while track space remains; at max Debt continue borrowing without advancing. New emergency Debt adds no current-turn expense; after loans Balance becomes zero. One or two loans lower Standing one, three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing; lower Standing one if short. Chairman may pay affordable dividends, one cash/share to each owner including self; if total paid strictly exceeds expectations, raise Standing one.

evidence.quote: At maximum Debt, keep taking loans without advancing Debt any further.

answers.answer: Company-directed Invasion/Rebellion first resolves the primary Crisis, then secondary Rebellions in every other unrest Company region, Bombay→Madras→Bengal; within a Presidency its Commander orders regions. Primary normal Crisis strength includes target unrest; Foreign Invasion primary uses ordinary attack die with no unrest; secondary strength is only that region's unrest. Associated Commander chooses/exhausts pieces; if vacant Military Affairs acts instead, and if both vacant Chairman chooses; substitutes gain/lose no trophies. Exhaust active pieces equal strength or as many as possible. Exact equality means attack fails/defense succeeds, clears all target unrest, actual Commander gains one trophy (substitutes none); if defeating normal primary Invasion remove one attacker tower if possible. Unequal means attack succeeds and Region Loss follows.

evidence.quote: Resolve attacks in this order: primary Crisis first

answers.answer: Voting support −1 or less fails: discard law, resolve dilemma If Failed, Opposition Leader takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one adjacent space and resolves it. Zero or higher passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes token, resolve selected policy then immediate law effects. Before voting PM moves dial clockwise or counterclockwise to first policy space matching law's bottom icon. Restore used vote cards after either result. Law-caused failure waits until vote ends before Final Scoring.

evidence.quote: −1 or less fails

answers.answer: In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call Deregulation if Standing and/or Debt on a lined space, and must if either on starred space. Ordinary voting threshold/procedure; no policy, PM may vote against. Pass: reduce Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, PM gets passed-law token, activate firms. Fail: increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token up to ±3 VP/share; PM stays and Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 begins deregulated.

evidence.quote: may call special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt on lined space

answers.answer: Form only if managing no firm: return eligible Company share to supply or flip workshop invested; flip board to firm charter, place family member as first share, set value to leftmost, take £5 from bank into London treasury. Invest with manager consent via Company-share/workshop contribution and £5 bank→London. Ten-share max; beyond it £5 still goes in but creates no share. Chairman share unusable; no Company shares while Standing and/or Debt on lined space; shares created this turn cannot be reinvested even after trade. Invested workshop never reverts, loses bonus/failure VP and stays invested after firm failure.

evidence.quote: take £5 from bank into the London treasury

answers.answer: Each firm gets one trade attempt/turn and needs a ship to select a strategy; may select closed home port. Secretly commit bid from London; reveal bids simultaneously, strategy at matching Presidency start. Roll one die per bid £, pay bank; at least one 1/2 enables trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful bid dice; President's successful Trade generates initiative similarly. Fill lowest initiative first; President decides ties (not automatic Company priority). If President vacant or doesn't succeed, firms fill after Commander/Governors, Chairman breaks ties. Fill open orders up to ships+1, from selected port along own route; each firm fills an order only once, but can refill another firm's/Company order and vice versa. Previously filled order pays half rounded-down revenue. Advance Value one per full £6 India treasury revenue added this turn.

evidence.quote: Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn.

answers.answer: At Revenue start firms pay £1/charter ship plus higher of share count or firm value, from either/both London and India. If unable, dissolve unless rescued: shares to Debtor's Prison (−1 each), ships to shipyards, charter to family side; workshops stay invested. After expenses manager may dividend from India only: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 manager. Waivers need shareholder choice and manager consent. Record total actual payout on Company Balance track; active non-Hobnob with no dividend records zero; Hobnob retains marker. Sweep remaining India cash to London.

evidence.quote: Pay £1 per charter ship plus higher of share count or firm value

answers.answer: Components are limited; if supply runs out complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies; Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. All information including discards and family cash is public except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids.

evidence.quote: Components are limited: when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible.

answers.answer: Tradeable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares, promise cards. Not tradeable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. Transfer a share by returning old owner's family member and replacing it at that location with a receiving-family member. Blackmail must remain facedown to trade; used faceup blackmail cannot be traded.

evidence.quote: Enterprises; facedown blackmail; family treasury cash; Company/firm shares; promise cards

answers.answer: Immediate transfers bind; future-behavior promises are nonbinding except a printed promise card's guaranteed effect can be called if possible. Calls follow card timing/limits; none during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which. Promise cards may be transferred to third party or guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (e.g. workshop bonus already paid this phase is not repeated after sale).

evidence.quote: Immediate transfer | Binding.

answers.answer: Use scenario player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six, shuffle and deal evenly. Place all listed holdings; starting luxuries each give 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together as one deck; deal three London display cards, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown. Scenario card sets map, finances, military etc.; initial player ships/offices also come from dealt cards.

evidence.quote: add three extra cards for five players or six for six players

answers.answer: Ends after scenario final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Usually failure is immediate; during India Events finish that phase before Final Scoring; legislation-caused failure finishes vote first. During all Final Scoring no negotiations or promise calls; after game over stop negotiations, promises and blackmail unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use.

evidence.quote: failure during Events finishes that phase, and legislation failure finishes vote before scoring

answers.answer: Power counts enterprises and Company shares at current Power rates (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, printed card power including blackmail faceup/down and applicable spouse. First/second awards: turns 1–3: 3/1; 4–6: 5/2; 7–8: 8/4. Tied first each get only lower award, nobody else gets one; tied second get none. Highest final VP wins; ties most windows, then clockwise from PM.

evidence.quote: Count enterprises and Company shares

answers.answer: Survived: add Court's current VP/share. Failed: subtract it/share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop (scores may be negative). Survived final outcome: roll office attrition then retire pensioners, no display cards. Failed: draw one random Company failure card instead. Firm special retirement is an earlier separate step in either outcome.

evidence.quote: If Company survived, add Court’s current VP per Company share.

answers.answer: Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot transfer; required enterprise/share trades occur immediately when taking spouse. Discounts stack, are personal and each usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual spending and display priority.

evidence.quote: Retirement discounts can stack, are personal

answers.answer: If returned by Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, fitted ship stays in play. Cannot purchase shipyard while its matching ship remains in play; may purchase after ship returns.

evidence.quote: its fitted ship stays in play

answers.answer: Enlist Writer: place member in any Presidency Writers box; with at least four vacant offices place one extra once this turn. Enlist Officer: member to Officers-in-Training. Luxury: pay bank £4, gain luxury, 2 VP while owned and window icon. Shipyard: bank £2, matching ship unfitted on yard, shipping enterprise/one vote/£1 bonus while fitted. Workshop: bank £5, manufacturing/two votes/£1 bonus, 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. Seek Share: place member on empty Stock Exchange queue space; pay bank £2, £3, £3, £4 or £5; applicant, not share yet.

evidence.quote: Purchase Luxury | Pay bank £4

answers.answer: If a required family piece cannot be placed from supply, take one from any of your prizes and lose its printed VP; also applies to firm-share creation. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

evidence.quote: If placing a family piece with none in supply

answers.answer: If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, putting a member from supply into office; if necessary and possible take one from a prize and lose its VP. If impossible, there is no Chairman.

evidence.quote: If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns

answers.answer: Chairman elects Chairman through shareholders; Director chooses current officeholder except Chairman/Governor (or any writer if all offices vacant); Chairman hires Shipping from any writer and Military Affairs from Presidential Commander, else any officer, else trainee. Director hires each President from a writer of that Presidency or its associated Governor. Associated President hires Governor from writer/officer in region (not Commander). Chairman hires China writer immediately on creation; Governor General replaces Director and is hired same way.

evidence.quote: Director of Trade | Chairman chooses

answers.answer: Repeated Special Envoy checks, £1 treasury/die, no penalty: success opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing overlay/card and Chairman immediately hires a writer. After all Envoys, Director may make up to two transfers of one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones (China once created). Cannot transfer during Envoy actions.

evidence.quote: May make repeated Special Envoy checks

answers.answer: Military Affairs may first make up to two transfers of an officer/regiment between Armies, staying top half; then assign every trainee to any Army top half; finally appoint Commanders. If vacancy or a family has more total pieces than current Commander's family, choose from families with most pieces; move selected officer to Commander slot and return previous Commander to top as officer. A tie with incumbent does not replace. Nepotism does not apply.

evidence.quote: Then assign every Officer-in-Training

answers.answer: Each President orders its Commander, Governors and its Trade; must give each an opportunity, but Commander/Governors may decline. Each position finishes before next and cannot be interrupted. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve alliance purchases.

evidence.quote: Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and its own Trade.

answers.answer: Trade does not exhaust ships. At Refresh writers on orders return to their associated Presidency Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; filled tokens and dividers return to supply. Fitted ships keep fatigue.

evidence.quote: Trade itself never exhausts ships.

answers.answer: At start of Commander operations, before Deploy, request President treasury funds for printed-price alliances; President must approve. Move purchased alliances active/top. Deploy or defense exhausts whole alliance to bottom; printed strength usable once and cannot be split among purposes. Refresh exhausts unused active alliances too; does not reactivate them.

evidence.quote: At the START of Commander operations

answers.answer: Company defense penalty is zero and no tower remains, so zero tower trophies. With no tower or faceup loot modifier use minimum loot equal to surviving participating officers +1 for Commander, distributed normally. Region must have unrest or closed order to make action have effect.

evidence.quote: Company defense penalty is zero

answers.answer: Each successful Build is one stage. With no partial ship, place partial ship in Governor's region; a later successful Build completes it into sea zone associated with Governor's President (two successes total). Commissioned regiment goes into Army associated with President; it has officer-like strength, loot paid to bank and no officer-loss rolls.

evidence.quote: Each successful Build performs one stage

answers.answer: Successful Envoy or Envoy to China law creates China; in either case Chairman immediately hires any writer. China treasury holds ships, not cash; Director/Shipping can send ships there. They count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal.

evidence.quote: Created by successful envoy or Envoy to China law

answers.answer: China gets only one attempt, including failed attempt (no retry), rolling one die per ship; do not attempt absent Company-controlled export icon. Success counts export icons in all Company-controlled regions only: Balance receives £4 per icon, Superintendent family receives £1 per icon from bank. Non-Company exports do not count; Company payment isn't flat £4.

evidence.quote: After Bengal, may attempt China Trade only ONCE

answers.answer: Governor General law makes all Governors pensioners, removes overlays and partial ships, returns Governor/Director cards to box; replaces Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue and adds ribbon overlay. Conquests thereafter create no Governors/overlays; printed symbols show control. Governor General hires Presidents, uses former Director treasury/turn position and has normal attrition. Skip Governor elimination on region loss.

evidence.quote: First Balance +£3 per Company region.

answers.answer: First add £3 Balance per Company region. Then repeat Govern checks paying £1 treasury/die, no penalty; every rolled 6 adds unrest to each Company region even on success, and failure adds one more unrest to each. Success gives Governor General family £1 from bank per Company region, then requires one benefit per region: complete Company ship into any sea zone incl. China; regiment to any Army; or £2 to Balance/any other office treasury (not own), adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices put unrest in different regions. At most one successful Govern/turn.

evidence.quote: Every 6 rolled adds one unrest to each Company region

answers.answer: Roll once per eligible player-owned ship: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink; sunk ship returns to yard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are exempt. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships use strategy sea zone; Hobnob ships exempt.

evidence.quote: Roll once per eligible ship

answers.answer: A writer on newly closed order returns to owner's supply; flip filled token to closed. If asked to close an order in fully closed region, Cascade by closing all open orders directly connected. If connected order already closed, close that region's northernmost open order; if none, it also Cascades. Each region can initiate one Cascade per tile but can receive multiple effects.

evidence.quote: Return any writer on a newly closed order to its owner’s supply

answers.answer: Turmoil closes northernmost open order in top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer in top-stack region and all bordering regions. Shuffle: March Elephant, shuffle event into remaining draw stack, separately shuffle discards and put on top; if draw stack empty, March last instead.

evidence.quote: If draw stack empty, March last instead.

answers.answer: Leader: top-stack sovereign region gains tower; dominated region instead rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

evidence.quote: Top-stack sovereign region gains one tower.

answers.answer: Peace on border: open orders connected across Elephant border and add tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant wholly inside region, instead open all its orders and remove unrest. Then March.

evidence.quote: If Elephant wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders

answers.answer: Sovereign attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier must be strictly greater than defender's whole empire strength. Success replaces defender flag with attacker's dominated flag; taking capital shatters its empire. Attacker without empire uses available capital/star and matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags. Failure removes one attacker tower.

evidence.quote: must be greater than defender’s whole empire strength.

answers.answer: Compare only rebelling region strength + modifier with sovereign capital strength; other empire regions don't count. Must be strictly greater, so tie fails. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all orders (Cascade if already closed); failure removes one tower from capital.

evidence.quote: Compare only rebelling region strength + modifier

answers.answer: Region Loss: Commander returns half family's trophies rounded up and member to supply; roll once per Army officer, each 6 removes it. Eliminate Governor: card to unused stack, fatigue/member to supply; remove overlay, partial Company ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion specified strength) and invasion flag. Control token returns to region £ loot side down, region symbol up; no future loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Close orders for normal Invasion or Cascade if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close. Standing loss escalates by count lost so far this turn: first −1, second additional −2, etc. Other Company regions are not lost automatically; resolve separately.

evidence.quote: Standing loss equals number of regions lost so far this turn

answers.answer: After successful Invasion Crisis move Elephant to successful capital; otherwise to top-stack region. Company region: fully inside. Dominated: point toward sovereign. Sovereign: point across shape-marked border; if neighbor already dominated by actor choose first clockwise not, or if all dominated use redirect-arrow border toward empire capital.

evidence.quote: After successful Invasion Crisis, move to successful capital

answers.answer: Storm die chooses targets: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms means all; no storm means top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve invasion/Company attack. Success closes all orders (Cascade if all closed), removes target flag and all matching flags if capital, restores dome if Company-controlled, sets towers to half attack die rounded down. March with circle only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region invaded. Foreign Invasion primary gets no unrest added; FAQ says ordinary die also determines half tower level.

evidence.quote: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal

answers.answer: PM must draw at least one, revealing sequentially. After one or two ordinary (non-dilemma) draws may stop or continue up to three total, then choose one revealed and discard others. Dilemma forces choosing it and ends drawing. Before voting move dial clockwise/counterclockwise to first policy space matching chosen law's bottom icon; it fixes target/consequence.

evidence.quote: PM must draw at least one law

answers.answer: Tax: each family pays bank £1 per owned target; unpaid targets return to supply, including Chairman. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each prize member; unpaid item/member returns. Bonus: bank pays family £1 per target owned. Power: swap target marker with next higher; if already highest swap any other pair.

evidence.quote: Each family pays £1 TO THE BANK per target it owns.

answers.answer: Each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes. Each card can vote only once during entire vote across rounds; rotate when used until resolution. PM may call another full round or stop after each; round with no votes ends voting. Restore cards after outcome.

evidence.quote: Each card’s votes may be used only once in the entire vote

answers.answer: A supporter may later oppose; after opposing cannot support during that vote. Opposition Leader is player with most opposition votes; tied current holder retains. With recipient consent may cast for someone already opposed or committing to oppose; add to their opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced 'Vote with my enterprises' promise.

evidence.quote: A player who voted for may later oppose

answers.answer: Pay upkeep separately per prize member even final turn; if unpaid return member and lose prize's printed VP. Final turn skips Refresh and goes to Final Scoring. Otherwise writers return to associated Presidency box; filled tokens/dividers and extra ships to supply; exhausted officers/regiments reactivate; active alliances exhaust and do not reactivate; fitted player ships keep fatigue; advance turn and start London Season.

evidence.quote: Pay printed upkeep separately for each family member on a prize.

answers.answer: Each firm shareholder may make one additional London Season retirement from supply (not Pensioners), regardless of firm count. Actual spending after spouse discounts cannot exceed highest total dividend marker of any firm they hold; printed cost may exceed with discount. No retirement if marker absent/zero. Otherwise normal retirement, including prestige eligibility. Final Scoring: after firm scoring, one special retirement from supply before ordinary scoring, regardless Company success/failure, no display cards.

evidence.quote: Each shareholder may make one additional retirement per London Season

answers.answer: Firm has London and India treasuries. Bank's £5 investment goes to London; London pays ship acquisition, bids, expenses; trade proceeds go India, which pays dividends/expenses. Family cash cannot transfer into/out of firms. Only specified investment, payout and expense procedures move funds.

evidence.quote: Investment cash always comes FROM THE BANK TO London.

answers.answer: Firms phase after Family share creation and before Hiring; investments in any order until no one wants more, then choose strategies. Manager resolves timing conflicts within a firm; PM between firms.

evidence.quote: After Family share creation, before Hiring

answers.answer: May fit from own or another player's shipyard only with yard owner's consent; £3 from firm's London to bank. May buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent: £3 unfatigued or £2 fatigued, paid into Shipping treasury. Cannot acquire Company or extra ships.

evidence.quote: must have that shipyard owner’s consent

answers.answer: Only player managing no firm may initiate hostile takeover, so managing another firm disqualifies. Needs consent of holders of majority of target shares. Transfer target ships, money and shares to own charter, copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

evidence.quote: Only a player who manages NO firm at all may initiate one

answers.answer: Managers need every shareholder's consent. Highest-value firm primary; tied value, players choose. Move all secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family side; negotiated share transfers allowed. If primary exceeds ten shares, return excess to their owners' supplies with those owners' consent. Binding immediate whole agreement; primary retains continuing value/dividend track.

evidence.quote: Managers negotiate with every shareholder’s consent.

answers.answer: Hobnob has no bid, trade or dividends; firm still pays expenses and retains prior dividend marker for retirement. Hobnob ships are exempt from storms.

evidence.quote: No bid, trade or dividends.

answers.answer: Yes. Emergency investments follow normal Company-share/workshop rules even if ten-share cap prevents creating shares: investment still pays expenses, loses any remaining cash and lowers Value one space per emergency investment. Same-turn shares remain ineligible to reinvest, even after trading away; Chairman share and shares under lined Standing/Debt restrictions remain unavailable. (The ten-share cap specifically allows cash contribution without new share.)

evidence.quote: even when ten-share cap prevents more shares

answers.answer: Emergency merger may be with only one other firm. Normal merger procedure/every involved shareholder consent applies. Other firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover endangered firm's unpaid expenses.

evidence.quote: only ONE other firm

answers.answer: All shareholders must consent. Same as insolvent dissolution: shares to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards, charter flips family side. Invested workshops stay invested for rest of game.

evidence.quote: All shareholders must consent.

answers.answer: Before ordinary Power/Court/outcome scoring, each player totals VP from all shares across firms and rounds that player's total down once; deduct 1 VP per own piece in Debtor's Prison. Per share: Value 1 −1; 2 zero; 3–4 ½; 5–7 1; 8–9 1½; 10 2. Then firm special retirement before ordinary scoring. Company's failure does not change firm-share scoring.

1710 turns 1–5, no deregulation procedures. 1758 turns 3–7, starts monopoly and can vote deregulation. 1813 turns 5–8, starts deregulated. Long 1710 turns 1–8, same initial as 1710 and deregulation available.

1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office £3, Royal Protection, one regiment/Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12, Debt 3, each office £4, Calico Acts, one regiment/Army, one Company ship East Indian, Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

evidence.quote: £10 expectations / 0

answers.answer: 1813: Standing £10, Debt 0, each office £3; Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor's Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments/Army, one Company ship/sea zone. Put +2/−2 share-value token in Court; create China; place Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens; return Governor General law to box, overlay it over Director of Trade; use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors.

evidence.quote: put +2/−2 share-value token in Court

answers.answer: Power awards for first/second: final turn 1–3 = 3/1 VP; 4–6 = 5/2; 7–8 = 8/4. Tied first players receive only the lower award each; no other award is made.

evidence.quote: 3/1 VP if final turn 1–3
